title: A New Story for Žižkov? Making Sense of Street Renaming in a Prague Neighborhood after Russia’s Invasion of Ukraine
abstract: This article examines the 2023 renaming of Koněvova Street in Prague’s Žižkov district as a case of late post-socialist mnemonic reconfiguration amid geopolitical tensions following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. Drawing on interviews with urban actors involved in the renaming and members of the local community, the study elucidates the interaction between authorised narratives and everyday meaning-making. The paper does so by revisiting Wulf Kansteiner’s (2002) understanding of collective memory production as a dynamic relationship between memory makers, memory consumers and discursive objects shaped by specific traditions of representation. The renaming has reconfigured the local symbolic landscape by combining the removal of a Soviet-associated figure with the introduction of a locally significant historical actor, an intervention invested with reparative potential. The mnemonic revision has thereby introduced a learning process with potential implications for community resilience. The findings, however, reveal heterogeneous responses, showing how public memory re-evaluation, as envisioned from above, encounters locally rooted understandings, attachments and senses of belonging. The article demonstrates how the intervention is interpreted divergently within locally embedded mnemonic frameworks and against a changing geopolitical context that has renewed the salience of Soviet commemorative legacies across the post-socialist region.
